☁
Specific yield = plant generation ÷ installed capacity (kWh/kWp for the selected period). CUF = generation ÷ (capacity × 24 × recorded days) × 100. A red anomaly marker means output is over 30% below the preceding moving-average window. These are screening indicators, not proof of a fault. Financial savings, payback and campus-demand coverage require verified tariff, installation-cost and KSEB consumption inputs; those values are not assumed.

CAMPUS SUSTAINABILITY SNAPSHOT

Clean energy powering a greener tomorrow

Every unit of solar electricity generated can reduce the need for grid electricity. The equivalents below are illustrative estimates calculated from the production records currently available in this dashboard.

—Total recorded solar generation across all three installations

How this connects to sustainability

Solar generation supports institutional sustainability goals in several complementary ways.

13

Climate action

Estimated avoided CO₂ emissions are calculated from the configured grid-emission factor.

7

Affordable and clean energy

On-campus solar contributes renewable electricity and helps the institution understand the share of demand met by clean energy. Add verified campus consumption data to calculate this share.

12

Responsible consumption and production

Tracking production supports energy awareness, better monitoring and informed decisions about electricity use.

6

Water stewardship

Avoided thermal-generation water use is a broad indicative estimate, not a site-measured saving.

4

Education and awareness

The dashboard turns real production records into a learning resource for students, staff and visitors.

11

Sustainable communities

Clean-energy monitoring helps demonstrate the campus contribution to a more sustainable built environment.

Calculation notes: Values are approximate equivalents, not direct measurements. Factors used: 0.71 kg CO₂/kWh; 0.55–0.70 kg coal/kWh; 21.8 kg CO₂ absorbed per mature tree per year; 1,200 kWh/year per household; 2.3 kg CO₂/litre of petrol; 0.12 kWh/km for EV driving; and 3–4 litres of thermal-plant water use per kWh. Tree equivalent means the annual CO₂ absorption of an equivalent number of mature trees—not trees planted or saved. Water figures vary significantly by generation technology and location. Review and cite authoritative sources for these factors before using them in formal reporting.
